g11-history-uh5-t1.overview: Ancient and Medieval African States sits inside Peoples and States of Africa to 1500. African states fill Unit 5 of Grade 11 History, aligned to the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the four language families of Africa and how they spread. Then North Africa under the Mamluks and the spread of Islam across the Maghreb. Next, the West African empires of Ghana, Mali, Songhai, and Kanem-Bornu. Also the Swahili coast, Great Zimbabwe, and the Khoi Khoi and San of the south. Finally, the Trans-Saharan trade that linked the regions of Africa. Students will also learn how these African states connect to African identity and heritage today.
objectives: Identify the major African states and their regions.
Locate the language families of Africa on a map.
Explain the wealth of the West African empires.
Compare Ghana, Mali, and Songhai in turn.
Describe the Swahili coast and Great Zimbabwe.
g11-history-uh5-t1.simple:
Ancient and Medieval African States in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the Niger-Congo, Afro-Asiatic, Nilo-Saharan, and Khoisan language families.
  • Then the many ancient and medieval African states across the continent.
g11-history-uh5-t1.detailed:
Ancient and Medieval African States — the essentials. First, the Niger-Congo, Afro-Asiatic, Nilo-Saharan, and Khoisan language families. Then the many ancient and medieval African states across the continent.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Identify the major African states and their regions.
  • Locate the language families of Africa on a map.
  • Explain the wealth of the West African empires.
  • Compare Ghana, Mali, and Songhai in turn.
  • Describe the Swahili coast and Great Zimbabwe.
